title: ReleaseHarnessAcceptedContract
description: The proposition release-harness adjudicates: a subject, what must hold of it, and the normative references whose change would alter that meaning. Deliberately excludes execution bindings, authoring metadata and acceptance metadata -- a proposition's identity must not move because a port changed or a different person accepted it.

id.description: Stable identifier for the subject. Chosen by the author, not derived from a directory name or any other local filesystem accident.

assertions.description: What must hold. A contract asserting nothing certifies nothing, so this must be non-empty.

requires.description: Normative references: other subjects whose change would alter what these assertions mean. Each must be pinned by digest -- an unpinned reference is a convention, not a reference.

id.description: Identifier unique within this contract. Verdicts cite it, so it must be stable.

kind.description: Which executor evaluates this assertion. Only kinds the harness can exercise may be accepted -- a promise nobody can check is refused while it is still a draft.

target.description: The SYMBOLIC name of the thing exercised -- 'api', 'web', 'db'. What this resolves to at run time is an execution binding, supplied per-run and deliberately not part of the contract. This is what lets one contract be authored on a laptop and certified in CI.

description.description: What this assertion means, in the author's words. Carried into reports so a failure reads as a broken promise rather than a failed probe.

expect.description: What must hold. Deliberately unconstrained HERE: the shape is determined by `kind` and enforced by the allOf rules below, which close it per kind. See assertion-kinds-v1.json.

allOf.description: An assertion of kind "http" may only expect what the http adapter reads.

expect.description: Exercise an HTTP endpoint. WHERE it lives is an execution binding; this says only what must be true of the response.

path.description: Path appended to the bound location. Defaults to /.

body_contains.description: Non-empty substring that must appear in the HTTP response body.

allOf.description: An assertion of kind "cli" may only expect what the cli adapter reads.

expect.description: Exercise a command. WHAT is executed comes from the execution binding -- an assertion never carries a command, because a command is a local fact about where things are installed, not part of a promise.

args.description: Extra arguments appended to the bound command.

stdout_contains.description: Substring that must appear in stdout.

stderr_contains.description: Non-empty substring that must appear in stderr. This is an author-written expectation; stderr never determines failure attribution.

ref.description: Identifier of the referenced subject or artifact.

digest.description: sha256 of the referenced proposition, pinning exactly which version this contract was accepted against.
